phase: W2b-3: sound and music in the browser host
change: NTSDWeb: WebAudioMixer renders OriginalMacSoundEffects (the effects mixer the SDL host's audio thread pulls) and the playing music tracks into a shared ring of interleaved stereo Float32 frames from a 10 ms main-queue timer, keeping ~150 ms queued (no audio threads on WASI); frames the page played short while the loop stalled (loading, a question, a long frame) or could not play (a suspended context) come back as owed and are rendered and dropped (at most 10 s at once), so effect voices and the music clock keep wall-clock time as on an audio thread; the effects are silent while the page is hidden or unfocused (DirectSound's foreground rule, as the other hosts apply it), music plays on. WebMusicPlayer is OriginalMacMusicOutput.Player for the packaged ALAC tracks: decoded packet by packet ahead of its position (OriginalALACDecoder, a streaming form of OriginalALACTrack.samples(), compiled for WASI only), linearly interpolated from 44.1 kHz to the context rate, linear volume as SDL_SetAudioStreamGain, ended once at the end as AVAudioPlayer; the decoder (and the compressed file) released when finished or failed. Scripted runs have no audio (the manifest's silent players, as before). Page: an AudioContext asked for 44.1 kHz (the tracks' rate; a 192 kHz device rate costs 4x the mixing) created on the start gesture, an AudioWorklet (web/audio.js) playing the ring (a power-of-two capacity of at least 0.35 s), resume() never awaited (a gamepad button, a touch or Esc is no activation) and retried on later clicks, releases and keys; the page's focus reported to the host; audio counters in the page report and as ntsdAudio() for --steps logs. web_run.mjs: --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required for automated Chromium runs. Package.swift: NTSDWeb depends on NTSDMusicDecoder; CALAC's TARGET_RT_LITTLE_ENDIAN also for .wasi.
bugsFoundInTesting: The vendored Apple ALAC decoder failed every packet on wasm32 (webMusicError corrupt("packet at 8192")): TARGET_RT_LITTLE_ENDIAN was defined only for Linux, Android and Windows, so the decoder byte-swapped its bitstream on WASI. A wasm32 probe of main.caf decoded whole and streamed now gives macOS's result: 21,295,872 samples, checksum 4510584050078320065, 2,600 packets.

Headless Chromium's default AudioContext ran at 192 kHz: the 16,384-frame ring held only 85 ms, below the 100 ms target, with 272 underrun quanta; the context now asks for 44.1 kHz and the ring is sized from the rate.
A second page variable named ring (the input ring) clashed with the sound ring (a SyntaxError caught by node --check before any run).

review: Round 1 (independent, read-only): high: the worker started only after audio.resume(), which stays pending without a user activation (a gamepad button, a touch, Esc), so such a start never ran; medium: focus silenced the music as well as the effects (the other hosts silence only DirectSound's effects); medium: the mixer, fed from the main loop, froze the music clock and voices during loads, questions and long frames, delaying the end of a track; low: a possible read past decoded samples after a decode failure, memory (decoder and file kept), far seeks decoding synchronously, the initial focus, the 'short by' check, stale comments. All fixed (owed frames for the clock) or documented (far seeks; the game seeks to 0). Round 2: OK; low items (touch release as WebKit's activation, autostart focus, the 10 s cap documented, the decoder released after a failure) fixed; the owed count's bounded error at a context state change documented.
boundaries: The music clock is the frames rendered, as with SDL's audio thread; stalls longer than 10 s leave it that much behind
New effects start up to ~150 ms (the queue) plus the output latency after the game asks
A far seek decodes on the main thread up to the target (the game seeks music to 0 only)
Sound in a player's own browser (devices, Safari) and gamepads are hand checks
